description: Native Zoom transcript pull (option C) - fetch Zoom cloud-recording transcripts via BYO-credentials OAuth, normalize them, and feed the existing mapping/upkeep pipeline. No recorder, no bot, no Recall. MIT-clean.

userStories.title: Add NormalizedTranscript model and ingestion adapter
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a source-agnostic transcript model and an entry point into the existing mapping/upkeep pipeline, since today only the local recorder's output can be ingested.
acceptanceCriteria: Define a NormalizedTranscript type: { meetingId, title, startedAt, segments: [{ speaker, startMs, endMs, text }] }

Add an ingestion function that accepts a NormalizedTranscript and drives the existing mapping -> de-dupe -> upkeep flow by reusing the recorder's downstream entry point (do not duplicate pipeline logic)
A hand-built NormalizedTranscript fixture passed to the ingestion function reaches the same mapping/upkeep code path as a recorder transcript
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add Zoom credential and token storage to local DB
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to persist the user's own Zoom OAuth app credentials and issued tokens locally so the app can authenticate to Zoom.
acceptanceCriteria: Add local DB storage for: zoomClientId, zoomClientSecret, zoomAccessToken, zoomRefreshToken, zoomTokenExpiresAt
Credentials and tokens are stored only in the local DB layer, never in committed config or repo files
Provide get/set accessors for these fields
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Zoom BYO-credentials OAuth connect flow and settings UI
userStories.description: As an OSS user, I want to register my own Zoom OAuth app and connect it so the desktop app can read my cloud recordings.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings UI has inputs for Zoom Client ID and Client Secret that save to local DB (US-002)
Implements OAuth Authorization-Code flow for a desktop app via loopback redirect (http://localhost:<port>/callback)
Requests scope cloud_recording:read
On success, exchanges the code and stores access/refresh tokens and expiry in local DB
Implements token refresh when the access token is expired
UI surfaces the exact redirect URI the user must add to their Zoom OAuth app
After connecting, a test call to a Zoom list-recordings endpoint returns HTTP 200
Verify in the running app that the connect flow completes and shows a connected state
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: List Zoom cloud recordings and locate the transcript file
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to list the user's recent Zoom cloud recordings and resolve the downloadable VTT transcript artifact for a chosen meeting.
acceptanceCriteria: Call the Zoom API to list the authenticated user's recent cloud recordings (title, date, meeting id)
For a selected recording, locate the recording file of type TRANSCRIPT and obtain its authenticated download URL
If the selected meeting has no transcript, return a clear 'no transcript available' result rather than throwing
Uses tokens from US-002 and refreshes via US-003 when expired
Tests pass

userStories.title: Parse Zoom VTT into NormalizedTranscript
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to convert Zoom's speaker-labeled VTT transcript into the NormalizedTranscript model.
acceptanceCriteria: Download the VTT from the URL resolved in US-004
Parse cue timestamps and speaker-name prefixes into ordered segments { speaker, startMs, endMs, text }
Produce a NormalizedTranscript (US-001) with correct named speakers and millisecond timestamps
Unit test parses a sample Zoom VTT fixture stored under test-transcripts/ to the expected segments

userStories.title: Manual 'Fetch from Zoom' trigger with state handling
userStories.description: As an OSS user, after a recorded Zoom meeting I want to click Fetch from Zoom, pick the meeting, and have its transcript pulled in and run through mapping/upkeep.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Fetch from Zoom' action lists recent recordings (US-004), lets the user pick one, then fetches (US-004) -> parses (US-005) -> ingests (US-001)
Handles and clearly messages each state: not connected, no recordings, no transcript on the meeting, expired/refreshing token, fetch error
On success the fetched meeting appears mapped/upkept in the app, identical to a recorder-sourced transcript
No state fails silently
Verify in the running app that an end-to-end fetch of a transcript-enabled recording appears in mapping/upkeep
Typecheck passes
